text:
maria: sec-bot alert — anomaly: analytics-sa appears bound to a cluster role allowing cross-namespace reads in prod. noticed weird access spikes to customer datasets. tagging @ops-oncall and @alex.

ivan: can you paste the alert and the binding name?

maria: alert payload below:
```\nAlert: RBAC Escalation Detected\nServiceAccount: analytics-sa@redwood.svc\nDetectedBindings: ClusterRoleBinding/analytics-sa-global-read\nTriggeredBy: rbac-generator v2 apply at 2026-03-19T23:12:05Z\nMatchedRule: generated cluster-scoped binding when namespace pattern=\"*\"\n```

maria: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding analytics-sa-global-read -o yaml` shows subjects: 
```\nsubjects:\n- kind: ServiceAccount\n  name: analytics-sa\n  namespace: prod-analytics\nroleRef:\n  kind: ClusterRole\n  name: global-data-reader\n```

jess: ack. first mitigation: remove the cluster-scoped binding and re-create a namespaced RoleBinding limited to prod-analytics, then revoke tokens. i'll start delete.

alex: before delete — is there any live job depending on cluster-scope? do we have a canary to flip to fallback?

maria: quick scan: cron jobs in prod-analytics that pull cross-namespace metrics might fail, but those are non-customer-facing. low risk.

ops-oncall: i'm on it. running: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding analytics-sa-global-read` now.

ops-oncall: deleted. confirmed no immediate 5xx spikes.

ivan: PR that caused this looks like GH: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3427|infra#3427> — generator defaulted `target_namespaces = ["*"]` when module var was unset. moving to revert.

maria: good catch. also need to rotate any long-lived SA tokens and revoke exec sessions. commands to run:
```\nkubectl -n prod-analytics get secrets | grep analytics-sa-token\nfor s in $(kubectl -n prod-analytics get secret -o name | grep analytics-sa); do kubectl -n prod-analytics delete $s; done\n```

jess: i've queued a serviceaccount rotation job and created a scoped RoleBinding: `rbac-prod-analytics-analytics-sa` with just `read: namespaced:datasets` + `get:secrets:own-namespace`.

alex: also found terraform state entry: module.rbac-generator.var.target_namespaces = ["*"] in the workspace for `infra/prod`. patching vars file to explicitly list prod namespaces and adding validation to refuse `*`.

maria: forensic queries — run this to look for dataset access after 2026-03-19T23:00Z:
```\nSELECT sa, dataset, access_time, action FROM audit_logs\nWHERE sa = 'analytics-sa' AND access_time >= '2026-03-19T23:00:00Z';\n```

ivan: results: 127 rows touching `customer_metrics_*` buckets, mostly read operations. flagged 3 accesses to restricted dataset `cust_pii_2025` — starting triage on those.

ops-oncall: temporarily added `analytics-sa` to denylist in KMS policy and disabled its access to KMS decrypt for all keys. that'll block decryption of any encrypted secrets if it tries to escalate.

maria: good. also scheduling a CMK rotation for keys used by prod-analytics, and creating an incident ticket for SOC review.

jess: PR to revert infra#3427 opened: <https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3430|infra#3430>. adding automated test to reject wildcard namespaces and to lint generator output.

alex: postmortem items so far: stricter var validation for rbac-generator, require explicit namespace list, add pre-apply dry-run checks comparing generated bindings vs allowed patterns, and add an emergency `denylist` RBAC policy that can be applied cluster-wide quickly.

maria: timeline for remediation: 
- 23:12 apply created bad binding (detected)
- 23:14 alert fired by sec-bot
- 23:16 clusterrolebinding deleted
- 23:20 tokens revoked, KMS deny applied
- 23:40 scoped RoleBinding created and infra PR reverted

ivan: i've captured evidence and exported audit logs to secure bucket `gs://sec-audit/2523456789/`.

ops-oncall: monitoring for anomalies for 24h. no new KMS decrypts from analytics-sa.

sec-bot: automated summary: incident containment complete. recommended next steps: full key rotation window, legal/COMMS check for PII exposure, update runbook, tag owners for follow-up.

maria: thanks all — leaving this thread open for final confirmations. :thumbsup:
